Thanks again for your time today, Tom and Priya — great conversation. Per request, here’s a short recap of the performance topics we covered and proposed next steps. I’ve attached a one-page draft SLO doc and a mutual action plan.

Recap (high level):
- Primary use case: customer-facing chat and transactional generation (100–300 token responses).
- Target traffic: pilot 200 rps, scale to 500 rps in Q3; peak burst expected ~800 rps for marketing events.
- Latency goals: 95th <= 120ms for 100-token generations (US), 95th <= 160ms (EU), soft target for APAC 200ms with regional routing.
- Concurrency: 40–60 concurrent active sessions, 100+ background inference pipelines for batch jobs.
- Streaming: required for chat UI (progressive token streaming), low-latency commit for initial tokens.
- Data residency: EU customer data must remain in EU region; APAC users prefer APAC region but some countries require on-prem or strict residency.

Questions / checkpoints we promised to follow up on:
1) Which endpoints need strict EU-only processing vs. allowed cross-region?
2) Any regulatory constraints that prevent routing APAC traffic to US in fallback scenarios?
3) Expected peak concurrent KV cache size (helps sizing dedicated pools).
4) Will you need SOC2 artifact access or a Private deployment (VPC) for pilot?

Next steps:
- I’ll share a short technical note with recommended regional routing configuration and SLO targets for your pilot. (attached: Finova_SLO_Draft_v1.pdf)
- Aditya will propose a dedicated capacity sizing and cost estimate based on the concurrency/throughput numbers.
- Rishi can join the next call to cover security and residency options.

Attachments: Finova_SLO_Draft_v1.pdf, Finova_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx

Thanks — talk soon.

—

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- EU residency: All PII for EU customers must be processed and stored in EU. That rules out routing EU requests to the US for processing.
- APAC: For Japan and Australia we’re OK with regional processing in APAC cloud regions. For markets like India we may need to keep data in-country; that could mean Private deployment or a partner-hosted region.
- Streaming: yes, streaming is a hard requirement for the chat UX. Initial token latency is most critical.
- Throughput: pilot target is 200 rps, target to scale to 500 rps in production. Concurrency estimate: 50 active sessions.

Can you confirm the following in the technical note:
1) Recommended multi-region routing strategy that enforces EU-only processing for EU users but provides low-latency failover within region for availability.
2) Expected 95th percentile latency numbers for each region under our pilot scale (200 rps) versus production (500 rps).
3) Outline of options if APAC country-level residency is required (Private deploy vs. partner).

Also looping in our security mailbox (security@finova.com) — they’ll want SOC2 details and evidence of data flows.

Thanks — Tom

Tom — thanks, very clear. Quick technical note below (I’ll also attach the PDF with a few charts). If you want, we can turn this into a short 30-min follow-up with Aditya and Rishi to validate numbers and run through residency options.

Short technical note (pilot 200 rps / production 500 rps)
1) Regional routing recommendation:
   - EU users: route to EU-hosted model endpoints only. No cross-region processing. Use EU regional KV cache and EU-dedicated pools.
   - US users: route to US-hosted endpoints. Primary region US-west (closest to your main traffic), failover to US-east for capacity spikes.
   - APAC users: prefer APAC region endpoints; if country-level residency is required, propose Private deployment or partner-hosted region in-country.
   - Fallback policy: within-region fallback only; cross-region failover allowed only for non-PII/non-customer-data endpoints (e.g., public content) with explicit opt-in.

2) Latency expectations (95th percentile, 100-token generation):
   - Pilot (200 rps): US ~ 90–120 ms, EU ~ 120–160 ms, APAC ~ 160–220 ms (depends on region/provider).
   - Production (500 rps): US ~ 110–150 ms with dedicated pools and batching tuned; EU ~ 140–180 ms; APAC ~ 180–240 ms.
   - Notes: streaming initial-token latency can be improved by smaller batch windows and aggressive prefix caching; we typically hit ~60–90 ms p50 for first token in US with streaming enabled.

3) Throughput & concurrency sizing:
   - For 200 rps pilot with 50 concurrent sessions we recommend a small dedicated pool (2–4 GPUs depending on model family & quantization) configured with continuous batching and a 100-token soft limit.
   - For 500 rps production target plan for 6–10 GPUs with autoscale headroom for bursts to ~800 rps. Exact GPU count depends on model variant and quantization. Aditya will size this precisely after you confirm model family and token distributions.

4) Streaming requirements:
   - Redwood supports token-by-token streaming to clients over HTTP/2 or WebSockets. We recommend enabling early flush for the first token and a small batch timeout (5–10ms) to preserve interactivity.

5) Data residency / compliance options:
   - Hosted (Redwood API) with regional endpoints: EU-only processing is enforceable at the routing layer and we persist EU data only to EU storage when configured.
   - Dedicated (reserved capacity) with EU-only hosts provides stronger isolation and predictable latency.
   - Private (VPC / on-prem) deployed in-country for strict residency. We can coordinate a partner-hosted option if you prefer managed local infra.

Attachments: Finova_SLO_Draft_v1.pdf (detailed charts), Finova_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx

Next step: propose a 30-min technical call next week with Aditya and Rishi to lock sizing and residency path. Available windows: Tue 3/17 10–12 PT or Wed 3/18 13–16 PT. Which works for you?

—
Marissa
